reuse.why: Uses the existing WeekendRule/applyWeekendRule/applyWeekendRuleToDay abstraction and adds a shared isHoliday, but applyWeekendRule now re-implements the date move instead of extending getDateWithSkippedWeekend, and the daily-skip rule is not put in a shared helper.

duplication.why: The weekend-or-holiday predicate is written three times (closure in getNextDate, closure in applyWeekendRule, inline in getDatesInRange), the daily filter is repeated twice in getNextDate, and getDateWithSkippedWeekend survives as a stale weekend-only copy of the move logic.

placement.why: Holiday matching and the move rule sit in shared/schedules.ts, but the daily-skip decision and the `skipWeekend && !isDaily` flag computation are made separately in getNextDate and in the new server handler.

scope.why: Changes match the four steps (daily skip, range handler, holidays, MM-DD entries) with tests; the import reorder and unused rrule data field are minor noise.

maintainability.why: The business-day rule and the daily-skip rule each live in several places, getUpcomingDates does not apply the daily skip at all, and a now-divergent getDateWithSkippedWeekend remains exported, so future rule changes will easily miss a copy.

bypasses_abstraction.where: applyWeekendRule no longer goes through getDateWithSkippedWeekend; server/schedules/app.ts getDatesInRange and shared getNextDate decide the daily weekend/holiday skip inline and pre-compute skipWeekend && !isDaily instead of the rule helper taking frequency.

disguised_duplication.where: The weekend/holiday move loop in applyWeekendRule restates getDateWithSkippedWeekend under a new shape, and the isNonBusinessDay closures in getNextDate and applyWeekendRule are renamed copies of the same predicate also inlined in getDatesInRange.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule gains `holidays`; getNextDate and app.ts getDatesInRange handle the daily skip themselves and pass `skipWeekend && !isDaily` into applyWeekendRule rather than the rule owning the daily case.
